title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover ordering (hysteresis + serialization)
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Fixes a race in the SLO enforcer that caused regional failover ordering thrashing during load-shedding. Adds hysteresis and serialized state transitions to stabilize failover decisions. Backported as emergency hotfix to main.
description:
Context and motivation:
During a recent incident, we observed the SLO enforcer rapidly flip regional failover decisions under bursty load and intermittent backend errors. The root cause was concurrent state transitions in the enforcer when multiple region-specific circuit-breaker events happened close together. This caused ordering instability and repeated failover/backoff cycles (thrashing), leading to higher latency and token loss for some requests.

What this PR does (single summary):
- Serialize region-level failover state transitions to ensure only one transition runs at a time per region.
- Add hysteresis/time-based backoff to prevent immediate re-failovers for the same region for a short window after recovery (configurable via sla.enforcer.hysteresis_ms).
- Prioritize queued failover operations to prefer global-tiered decisions (control-plane requests > automatic SLO triggers) to avoid starvation during bursts.
- Add telemetry: new metrics slo_enforcer.failover_attempts, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_skips, slo_enforcer.transition_queue_length and traces for transition lifecycle.
- Add unit tests and an integration canary that simulates concurrent circuit-breaker trips across regions.

Commits (high-level):
- Serialize enforcer transitions and add transition mutex per-region (Priya Shah)
- Hysteresis window implementation + config (Priya Shah)
- Priority queue for enforcer operations (Mateo Garcia)
- Add metrics + tracing spans (Arjun Patel)
- Tests: unit + canary simulation harness (Priya Shah)
- Docs: release note + config doc (Nicole Park)

Files changed (high-level):
- services/slo-enforcer/src/enforcer/region_state.rs (main logic, +200/+40)
- services/slo-enforcer/src/enforcer/hysteresis.rs (new) (+70/+4)
- services/slo-enforcer/src/enforcer/queue.rs (priority queue) (+60/+8)
- services/slo-enforcer/tests/ (new integration canary harness) (+30/+2)
- observability/metrics.yml (add new metrics) (+10/+1)
- docs/enforcer-config.md (document hysteresis config) (+8/+5)
- ci/canary.yml (add canary job) (+32/+68)

Design notes and rationale:
- We found the simplest reliable approach was to serialize transitions at the region granularity. That keeps the critical path small and avoids global coordination overhead. A per-region async mutex gates transitions and ensures idempotent retry semantics are safe.
- Hysteresis window default is 30s (configurable). This prevents immediate oscillation when transient errors resolve quickly. For heavy multi-tenant customers this can be tuned per-route using existing SLO policy overrides.
- Priority queue ensures that operator-initiated control-plane actions (manual overrides, canary rollouts) are not delayed or starved by automated retries. This was important in the incident where automated retries blocked operator rollback attempts.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover mutex/serialization correctness and hysteresis window behavior.
- Integration canary simulates 1000 concurrent requests with region A/B circuit-breaker trips; run in perf-canary against a staging cluster (job: ci/canary.yml).
- Local fuzz harness used to reproduce the reported thrashing pattern.
- Load test: 5m soak in staging with synthetic error injection showed no more than 1 failover per 60s per region under the repro pattern (previously ~12 in 2m).

CI / checks:

- integration canary: initially failed due to flakiness in test harness (timeout); fixed by increasing canary timeout and adding retry helper (in this PR). After rerun all checks passed.

Review conversation (summary):

- Priya Shah (author): "Addressed: docs/enforcer-config.md added; metrics use tagged region but cardinality limited via tagging policy documented in observability/metrics.yml."

Risk and rollback plan:
- Risk: hysteresis window mis-tuned could delay legitimate failovers. Mitigations: default conservative short window (30s) and per-tenant overrides; alerting added when transitions are skipped due to hysteresis (slo_enforcer.hysteresis_skips).
- Rollback: revert is trivial via git revert of the squash merge. We will monitor canary and production for 2 hours post-merge. If regressions occur, we will rollback and escalate.

Merge outcome:
- All reviewers approved. CI green after rerun. Merged to main via squash-and-merge. Backported branch: release/2026-02-stability (cherry-picked commit).
